title: Noise Control By-law No. 6555
edition: Consolidated for convenience only to May 20, 2025 (amended to include By-law No. 14340, 14342)

values.quote: By-law No. 6555, the Noise Control By-law
(Consolidated for convenience only to May 20, 2025)
In a quiet zone, a person must not make ... continuous sound, the sound level of which:
exceeds a rating of 55 dBA on an approved sound meter when received at a point of reception within a quiet zone
exceeds a rating of 45 dBA on an approved sound meter when received at a point of reception within a quiet zone
exceeds a rating of 60 dBA on an approved sound meter when received at a point of reception within a quiet zone
exceeds a rating of 55 dBA on an approved sound meter when received at a point of reception within a quiet zone
exceeds a rating of 70 dBA on an approved sound meter
exceeds a rating of 65 dBA on an approved sound meter

values.blank_context: 'background noise' credited only for commercial premises (s.___(b))
values.quote: exceeds 3 dBA above the background noise on an approved sound meter

unsupported_wording: Consolidation date: source prints 'May 20, 2025', not July. Also the claim omits intermediate→quiet (60 day / 50 night, s. 2.2(a)(i),(b)(i)) and quiet→other (60 / 55, s. 2.1(a)(ii),(b)(ii)) — not wrong, but incomplete. 'No ambient credit for equipment' is an inference: the by-law uses 'background noise' only in s. 3.1(b)(i),(iii) (amplified/live sound, commercial premises incl. extended-hours liquor establishments); it does not state an explicit rule for equipment.
note: Equipment-related numbers printed elsewhere: power equipment 77 dBA daytime (s. 3.1(e)); emergency generator testing exempt if continuous level does not exceed 80 dBA (s. 4.1(c)). No section on air conditioners or heat pumps.
